---
title: "Setup"
---

This page gets your environment ready to run the workshop notebooks.

**You only need to follow the recommended setup below.** It requires no Python
installation, gives you a full editor, and is easy to customize later. The other
options are collapsed at the bottom — only open them if the recommended path
doesn't fit your situation.

## Recommended: VS Code + Dev Container {#recommended}

This combines [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) with a ready-to-run
Docker environment. Everything (Python, TVBO, the simulator backend) is
pre-installed in the container, so there is **nothing to install or compile**
yourself — and because it's a real workspace, you can edit notebooks and add
packages whenever you like.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What you get
A working environment in a few clicks: open the project in VS Code, let it build
the container once, and start running notebooks. No `pip`, no virtual
environments, no version conflicts.
:::

### 1. Install the two tools

| Tool | Link |
|---|---|
| **Docker Desktop** (start it after installing) | <https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/> |
| **VS Code** | <https://code.visualstudio.com/> |

Then add the **Dev Containers** extension in VS Code: open the Extensions panel
(`Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + X`), search for **Dev Containers**, and install the one by
Microsoft (`ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers`).

### 2. Get the workshop materials

```bash
git clone https://github.com/virtual-twin/Brain-Simulation-Workshop
```

No Git? Download the repository as a ZIP from the
[workshop repository](https://github.com/virtual-twin/Brain-Simulation-Workshop)
(green **Code** button → **Download ZIP**) and unzip it.

### 3. Open it in the container

1. In VS Code, choose **File → Open Folder…** and select the workshop folder.
2. VS Code detects the dev container config and shows a prompt in the
   bottom-right: **Reopen in Container** — click it.
   *(No prompt? Open the Command Palette with `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + P` and run
   **Dev Containers: Reopen in Container**.)*
3. The first time, VS Code pulls the pre-built image. This can take a few
   minutes — afterwards it's instant.

### 4. Run a notebook

Open any notebook under `notebooks/`, select the suggested Python kernel if
prompted, and run the cells. You're set.

::: {.callout-note}
## Customizing later
You're in a normal VS Code workspace, just running inside the container. Install
extra packages from the integrated terminal (`pip install <package>`), edit the
notebooks, or add VS Code extensions in `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` and
rebuild. Your changes to files in the project persist on your machine.
:::

## Other options

Only need these if the recommended setup doesn't work for you (e.g. you can't
install Docker, or you want everything in the browser). Click to expand.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Docker only — Jupyter Lab in your browser

Use this if you're comfortable with Docker and don't want to use VS Code. It runs
the same pre-built environment, served as Jupyter Lab.

**Step 1.** Install [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/) and start it.

**Step 2.** Run Jupyter Lab:

```bash
docker run -p 8888:8888 -e MODE=jupyter ghcr.io/virtual-twin/tvbo:latest
```

**Step 3.** Open <http://localhost:8888> in your browser.

To keep your work across sessions, mount a local folder:

```bash
docker run -p 8888:8888 -e MODE=jupyter -v "$PWD/notebooks:/home/tvbo/notebooks" ghcr.io/virtual-twin/tvbo:latest
```
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Local install with uv

Use this if you prefer to work directly on your machine without Docker, or want
to install your own packages alongside TVBO.

### 1. Install uv

`uv` is a fast Python package manager that also handles Python installation.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### macOS / Linux

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

Restart your terminal afterwards (or run `source ~/.bashrc` / `source ~/.zshrc`).

#### Windows

Open **PowerShell** and run:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
```

Restart PowerShell afterwards.

If you get an execution policy error when running scripts later (e.g. activating the venv), allow signed local scripts for your user once:

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser
```

:::

Verify:

```bash
uv --version
```

### 2. Install Python

TVBO requires Python 3.11 or later. Install it with uv:

```bash
uv python install 3.12
```

### 3. Create an environment

```bash
mkdir tvbo-workshop
cd tvbo-workshop
uv venv --python 3.12
```

Activate it:

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### macOS / Linux

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
```

#### Windows

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\activate
```

:::

Your prompt will show `(.venv)` when the environment is active.

### 4. Install TVBO + TVB-Optim

```bash
uv pip install "tvbo[all]"
```

This installs TVBO and the TVB simulator backend used in the workshop.

### 5. Verify

Paste this directly into your activated shell (PowerShell, bash, or zsh):

```bash
python -c "from tvbo import Dynamics, SimulationExperiment; print('Ready!')"
```
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Google Colab — run in the browser, no install

Run the notebooks in your browser. No install required.

**Step 1.** Open a notebook in Colab:

- Click the **Open in Colab** button at the top of any notebook page on this site, or
- Download the `.ipynb` from the [workshop repository](https://github.com/virtual-twin/Brain-Simulation-Workshop) and upload it in Colab via *File → Upload notebook*.

**Step 2.** Run the first cell. It detects Colab and installs the dependencies. If a later cell fails with `ModuleNotFoundError`, install the missing package in a new cell:

```python
!pip install "tvbo[all]"   # or whichever package is missing
```
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## EBRAINS Collaboratory

EBRAINS provides JupyterLab through the [Collaboratory](https://wiki.ebrains.eu/bin/view/Collabs/). It works, but RAM is limited.

**Step 1.** Log in at [lab.ebrains.eu](https://lab.ebrains.eu) and start a JupyterLab session.

**Step 2.** Open a terminal and install TVBO into a user environment:

```bash
pip install --user "tvbo[all]"
```

**Step 3.** Upload the notebook you want to run and execute it. If you hit memory errors or import conflicts, switch to one of the other options.
::::

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| **Reopen in Container** prompt never appears | Open the Command Palette (`Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + P`) and run **Dev Containers: Reopen in Container**. Make sure the Dev Containers extension is installed and Docker Desktop is running. |
| Container build fails or hangs | Confirm Docker Desktop is running, then retry. The first pull downloads a large image — give it a few minutes on a slow connection. |
| Docker: port already in use | Change the host port: `docker run -p 8889:8888 ...` and open `localhost:8889` |
| `uv: command not found` | Restart your terminal; on macOS/Linux check that `~/.local/bin` is on your `PATH` |
| `No module named tvbo` | Activate the virtual environment first — you should see `(.venv)` in your prompt |
| Python version error | Run `uv python install 3.12`, then `uv venv --python 3.12` |
| Windows execution policy error | Open PowerShell as Administrator and run `Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser` |
